correctness.rationale: The lower bound is the explicit seven-word code, and complete exact enumeration verifies received-word multiplicity at most two. The upper bound is a finite rational dual certificate: all 64 length-six ambient words satisfy the pointwise inequality; summing uses only the definition that each length-four output belongs to at most two codewords. Exact arithmetic gives 36/5<8, so integrality forces at most seven.

value.rationale: The parameter is a natural finite instance of the list-deletion hypergraph rather than an arbitrary slice: \(\(k=t=2\)\) is the central pre-existing list-decoding case in Guruswami--Hastad and Lin. An exact \(\(n=6\)\) benchmark supplies a reproducible extremal datum and a compact rational certificate, useful for calibrating finite behavior against asymptotic bounds and for testing future constructions. The result is not merely a solver output or a recomputation of a known table.
